prompt: Where do the virtual machines of a classic Databricks cluster run?

choices.text: In Databricks' own Azure account, next to the control plane
choices.why: That is where the control plane and serverless compute run.

choices.text: In your subscription
choices.why: Right. In a managed resource group, or in subnets of your own network, billed to you by Azure.

choices.text: Inside the storage account that holds the lake
choices.why: A storage account holds data, not machines.

choices.text: On whichever region Databricks chooses that night
choices.why: Clusters run in the workspace's region.

prompt: An engineer tries to resize a disk on one of the cluster machines in the workspace's managed resource group, and Azure refuses, though she owns the subscription. Why?

choices.text: Her role is missing a permission for disks
choices.why: An owner has every permission an Azure role can give.

choices.text: The machine is running, and disks change only when it is stopped
choices.why: The refusal is about who may change it, not when.

choices.text: A deny assignment protects what Databricks manages, owners included
choices.why: Right. A machine fixed by hand is a cluster that fails for no visible reason.

choices.text: The managed resource group belongs to another tenant
choices.why: It is in her subscription, and her tenant.

prompt: A year after creating its workspace, Quitanda decides the clusters must run inside its own virtual network, with no public addresses. What does that take?

choices.text: Adding two subnets to the existing workspace's settings
choices.why: Injection cannot be added to a workspace after it is created.

choices.text: A new workspace, created injected, and the work moved to it
choices.why: Right. VNet injection is decided at creation, which is why the declaration has it from the start.

choices.text: A peering between the managed network and Quitanda's
choices.why: Peering connects networks; the machines still get public addresses.

choices.text: Switching the workspace to the trial tier
choices.why: The tier changes prices and features, not the network.

prompt: Unity Catalog needs a workspace on the ___ tier.
What is `azurerm_databricks_access_connector` for, in the declaration?

choices.text: It connects the workspace's two subnets to each other
choices.why: Subnets of one network reach each other already.

choices.text: It holds a managed identity that Unity Catalog uses to reach the lake
choices.why: Right. No storage key is handed to Databricks.

choices.text: It stores the token that Databricks' own Terraform provider signs in with
choices.why: It holds an identity for storage, not a token for the API.

choices.text: It gives the clusters a public address for the control plane
choices.why: `no_public_ip = true` says the opposite.

prompt: `terraform validate` accepted the workspace. Which of these could still fail when the file is applied to a subscription?

choices.text: A tier spelt `gold`
choices.why: That one validate already refused.

choices.text: Subnets too small for the machines, or a name already taken
choices.why: Right. Those are Azure's checks, at `apply`.

choices.text: A file not laid out as `terraform fmt` would
choices.why: Layout never fails an apply; `fmt -check` already passed.

choices.text: `no_public_ip` written as a string
choices.why: A wrong type is refused by validate.

prompt: A team wants its clusters, jobs and grants declared in Terraform too. Why can the file of this lesson not hold them?

choices.text: Databricks' own provider declares them; `azurerm` cannot reach them
choices.why: Right. Two providers: `azurerm` for the workspace, `databricks/databricks` for what is inside.

choices.text: Clusters cannot be declared in any tool at all, and are only ever clicked
choices.why: Databricks' provider declares them.

choices.text: They would make the file too long for validate
choices.why: Length is not the issue.

choices.text: Grants belong to Entra ID, not to the workspace
choices.why: Unity Catalog's grants are kept by Databricks.

prompt: Match each kind of Databricks compute to what it is for.
hint: Who uses it, and for how long?

pairs.right: Notebooks that people work on, shared
One run of a job, then terminated
SQL from analysts and BI tools
Warm compute in Databricks' account, billed in DBUs alone

right_distractors: A copy between two storage accounts

prompt: Where should Quitanda's nightly cleaning notebook run?
hint: Nobody is attached to it at three in the morning.

choices.text: On the all-purpose cluster the analysts use during the day
choices.why: That pays the all-purpose rate and shares a cluster with people.

choices.text: On a job cluster created for the run
choices.why: Right. It exists for the half hour it needs, at the jobs rate.

choices.text: On a SQL warehouse, since the rules are SQL
choices.why: A warehouse serves queries; a notebook job runs on cluster or serverless compute.

choices.text: On a pool, with no cluster at all
choices.why: A pool lends machines to clusters; it runs nothing itself.

prompt: What does a pool of idle machines cost, according to Databricks' documentation?
hint: Two bills, and only one of them stops.

choices.text: Nothing, until a cluster takes a machine
choices.why: Azure still bills the idle machines.

choices.text: DBUs and machines, as if they were running a cluster
choices.why: Idle pool machines are not billed in DBUs.

choices.text: Azure's price for the machines, with no DBUs
choices.why: Right. A little money for a lot of start-up time.

choices.text: Only DBUs, since the machines belong to Databricks
choices.why: In classic compute the machines are yours, in your subscription.

prompt: A job must finish by six in the morning, and the team wants Spot machines to save money. Where do they put them?
hint: What does losing each machine cost?

choices.text: On the driver, which works least
choices.why: Losing the driver loses the run.

choices.text: Everywhere, since Spark reruns whatever is lost
choices.why: It reruns tasks of lost workers, not a lost driver.

choices.text: On workers only, with the driver on an ordinary machine
choices.why: Right. A lost worker costs time; a lost driver costs the job.

choices.text: Nowhere; Spot is not available to Databricks
choices.why: Workers can be Azure Spot machines.

prompt: The setting that stops an all-purpose cluster after a number of idle minutes is called auto ___.

Five machines, each consuming an illustrative 1 DBU an hour, run 30 minutes a night for 31 nights on a job cluster. At an illustrative 0.30 USD per DBU and 0.20 USD per machine-hour, what is the month in USD, to two decimals?
Why did the all-purpose cluster that stops after 60 idle minutes cost four and a half times the job cluster, for the same work?

choices.text: All-purpose machines are larger
choices.why: The lesson used the same machines in both.

choices.text: Three times the hours, each at a higher DBU rate
choices.why: Right. An idle hour a night, and the all-purpose rate on every hour.

choices.text: All-purpose clusters are billed for the whole month
choices.why: Only the one never stopped was.

choices.text: Auto termination adds a fee of its own
choices.why: It saves money; it has no fee.

prompt: A team runs a few short jobs a night and pays for start-up minutes and an idle tail on each. What does serverless change in that bill?

choices.text: Nothing; serverless is the same compute at the same price
choices.why: It bills differently: DBUs only, for the work.

choices.text: It removes the DBUs and keeps the machine cost
choices.why: The reverse: the DBUs include the machines.

choices.text: It is free below a number of jobs a night
choices.why: No such allowance is documented here.

choices.text: It bills only the work, in DBUs at its own price
choices.why: Right. Whether it is cheaper depends on the two prices.

prompt: In `quitanda_prd.sales.orders`, what is `sales`?

choices.text: The catalog
choices.why: The catalog is `quitanda_prd`.

choices.text: The schema
choices.why: Right. Catalog, schema, table.

choices.text: The metastore
choices.why: The metastore has no part in the name.

choices.text: The external location
choices.why: Locations are paths, not parts of a table's name.

prompt: Somebody drops the external table `quitanda_prd.sales.orders`. What happens to its files in the lake?
hint: Who owns an external table's files?

choices.text: They stay; only the name goes
choices.why: Right. Dropping a managed table would delete its files.

choices.text: They are deleted at once, with the table
choices.why: That is a managed table.

choices.text: They move to the metastore's storage
choices.why: Nothing moves them.

choices.text: They become unreadable until the table is restored
choices.why: The files are untouched and readable by whoever may read the path.

prompt: The analysts must read `quitanda_prd.sales.orders` and nothing else. Which grants do they need? Choose all that apply.
hint: Each level has to let them in.

choices.text: `USE CATALOG` on `quitanda_prd`
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: `USE SCHEMA` on `quitanda_prd.sales`
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: `SELECT` on the table
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: `SELECT` on the schema `quitanda_prd.sales`
choices.why: That reaches every table in it, present and future: more than the orders.

choices.text: A data role on the storage account
choices.why: That reads the files around Unity Catalog, every column of them.

prompt: Quitanda has granted carefully in Unity Catalog, and a partner's tool still reads the customers' tax numbers from the lake. What is the likeliest way in?
hint: What does Unity Catalog never hear of?

choices.text: A bug in the column mask
choices.why: Masks apply to every engine reading through Unity Catalog.

choices.text: A key or SAS that reads the storage account directly
choices.why: Right. A read around the catalogue sees every file; keys disabled close that door.

choices.text: The metastore being in another region
choices.why: Region has nothing to do with who may read.

choices.text: A grant on the catalog given to the analysts
choices.why: The partner is not an analyst; that grant does not reach them.

prompt: An external location pairs a path in the lake with a storage ___, which wraps the access connector's identity.
hint: The other object on the right of the figure.

prompt: Put these from the outermost to the innermost.
hint: A name has three parts, and something holds them all.

prompt: Which of these is billed by Azure, not by Databricks, when a classic job cluster runs?
hint: The second line of a classic bill.

choices.text: The DBUs of the run
choices.why: DBUs are Databricks' line.

choices.text: The Unity Catalog grants
choices.why: Grants are not billed.

choices.text: The virtual machines
choices.why: Right. Classic compute pays Azure for them.

choices.text: The control plane's web application
choices.why: It is part of what DBUs pay for; nobody bills it separately.
